## Overview

**In plain terms.** Did the children offered the intervention express more in the Action Picture
Test than those who were not — and how large, and how certain, is that difference?

The Action Picture Test (Renfrew 1997) is an expressive-language measure that the project's causal diagram already treats as a direct outcome of randomised assignment (`IG -> {EI, EG}`), but which had no confirmed test ceiling until the manual maxima were supplied on 2026-08-18 — Grammar 37, Information 40. Until then it sat under "Deferred / follow-ups" in the ITT suite design note, and no Bayesian estimate existed for either scale.

Information awards half marks on some items, so the raw 0–40 score is not an integer count and a Beta-Binomial likelihood rejects it. The modelled outcome is the **doubled half-mark scale, out of 80** (`aptinfo_x2`). Doubling is exact — every observed fractional part is 0.5 — and preserves the proportion, so the logit mean structure is unchanged. It does assert 80 exchangeable trials where there are 40 partial-credit items, which overstates per-child precision; the Beta-Binomial concentration absorbs part of that, and [LRPITT129](../lrp-rli-itt-129/) is the registered out-of-40 comparator.

LRPITT029 estimates the assigned-arm contrast in the post-score among children in the fitted
observed-data analysis set, using the randomised phase only (time 1 $\rightarrow$ time 2).
Randomisation created exchangeability in the full randomised cohort, but conditioning on archive
inclusion and observed analytic variables can break it, so a causal reading of the fitted
contrast requires that selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and
potential outcomes.

_Identification and sign convention._ Under the locked DAG $G$ is a randomised root, so the
offer contrast needs no baseline-covariate adjustment; the own baseline $\gamma_{\text{own}}$
and linear age $\gamma_A$ are **precision terms only**. Attendance is never conditioned on (a DAG
collider). **Sign convention:** $G = 1$ is the intervention arm, so a **positive** $\tau$ means the
intervention arm has the higher modelled outcome.

## Model

$$
\eta_i = \alpha + \tau\, G_i
       + \gamma_{\text{own}}\, \text{logit}_*(EI_{\mathrm{pre},i}, N)
       + \gamma_A\, A_{\text{std},i},
$$

with Beta-Binomial likelihood, $\mu_i = \sigma(\eta_i)$, $N = 80$. Priors follow the shared
template in `priors.py`.
